MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 25, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:01 p.m., on January 25, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on January 20, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell (arrived at 5:30 pm)
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:30 pm)
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs (arrived at 5:30 pm)
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PUBLIC HEARINGS

1.  Presentation of the Six Proposed Voting District Maps Received by the City

  Mayor Bucknum opened the Public Hearing at 6:05 p.m.

City Council Minutes  1  January 25, 2022
   City Attorney Bill Curley outlined that tonight’s hearing is to introduce and assess the six
  proposed maps that were received within the specified time frame. Map A was prepared by
  CDR and five maps were prepared by members of the public. He outlined the timeline and
  procedure for the hearing.

  Deborah Diep presented all six maps to the City Council.

  City Attorney asked Deborah if she received any direction of addressing where incumbents
  live or if she knows where they live on Map A or in any analysis of the other maps. Deborah
  Diep stated for full disclosure that CDR did not know where the Council Members live when
  creating Map A

  City Attorney Bill Curley clarified that under the Fair Maps Act is the State Law that came
  into effect recently and did not apply to the 2018 mapping process. The prior maps were done
  under the 2010 Census. The maps presented are from the 2020 Census with fresh information
  in the sense of following the Fair Map Act and the new census data. The old information is
  no longer applicable.

  Mayor Bucknum opened the public comments portion of the Public Hearing. The following
  spoke:

  Aaron Hand, M.V.: Expressed that all five council districts should be up for re-election based
  on the stipulated agreement the city agreed to. Felt that the Citizen Voting Age Population
  (CVAP) of Latino voters in districts 4 and 5 on Map A dilutes the Latino vote and he
  encourages the Council to look at that issue. Stated that Map E District 1 provides the
  strongest Latino vote and asked that the City Council look at this map. Lastly, he pointed out
  that the City refused to provide the public with communications with CDR and refused public
  records requests which would allow the public to see what the City told CDR to do.

  Walt Lawson, M.V.: Asked the City Attorney if the resident lawsuit recently filed with the
  Attorney General on the 2018 two-year terms of Council Members Bucknum, Raths, and
  Sachs happens to be referred to the Superior Court of Orange County and the court decision
  is the removal from office, what will be the result of the district maps chosen by these Council
  Members and will it be valid. He commented on Map Z submitted from 2018 by CDR, and
  questioned Map A. Lastly, he discussed the map he turned in. He stated that his map has a
  20.5% CVAP of Hispanic voters in District 1 and his percentage spread on Map C is 2.46%.
  He agrees that Map E would be a very good map.

  Edward Maurer, M.V.: Commented on Map A that the area bordering Lake Forest is
  splitting Latino voters and is in favor of Map E.

  Aramis Vela, M.V.: Stated he is the author of Map E that he entitled the Latino Opportunity
  Plan. He outlined his map and stated that in District 1 this map has the highest Latino CVAP
  at 21.4%. He reported that this is significant because it will provide voting power for
  Hispanics in that district. Finally, he stated that the percentage spread between districts is a
  reasonable 4.6% well under the limit of 10%.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the City Council and the City Attorney on the districting
  process. Questioned how only three districts will be up for re-election in 2022 as announced
City Council Minutes  2  January 25, 2022
   by Mayor Kelley at the September 14 City Council Meeting. She asked how that can be
  decided when the district map has yet to be finalized. Suggested the process of the tile system
  in which numbered tiles are drawn out of a bag and the first three numbers drawn will be the
  districts designated for a four-year term, the remaining two tiles will be the districts designated
  for a two-year term. She felt that by disclosing the census block numbers of the Council
  Member residence would have given the public confidence in the process. Questioned the
  transparency of how decisions were being made.

  Mary Michael, M.V.: Asked the City Council to consider Map D and if not Map D, then
  Map E.

  Judy Fike, M.V.: States that she supports Map E because it fulfills the court order to protect
  the minority vote.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Discussed his district map he created in 2018 and questioned if the City
  Council should be making the final map decision. He stated that it is a conflict of interest for
  the City Council to choose the map.

  Ilene Geiger, M.V.: She agrees that all five Council seats should be up for re-election.
  Stated she is not in favor of Map A because it doesn’t resolve the issue of the violation of
  voting rights. She is in favor of Map E.

  Jon Miller, M.V.: He feels Map E makes the most sense because all of the neighborhoods
  are contiguous on Los Alisos. Stated if we are trying to get minority representation Map E
  seems to be the best map. Lastly, he agrees that someone other than the City Council should
  decide on the final map.

  The Council took no action and Mayor Bucknum closed the Public Hearing at 6:45.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked the Demographer on Map E District 1if she could smooth the
  district lines.

  Deborah Diep agreed to revise the map and stated that it would be Map E revision 1.

  Mayor Bucknum asked the Demographer for an analysis of Map E and Map A in regards
  to the minority vote percentage differences.

  Council Member Goodell asked the City Attorney to clarify that you can’t draw maps based
  on race.

  City Attorney stated that the law is clear both State and Federal Voting Rights Act that we
  cannot discriminate based on race. Equally as a given we can not use government voting
  structures to minimize, exclude any minority group whether it be race, ethnicity and age. We
  look to the State’s direction of the Fair Map Act which laid out the primary criteria. With
  having said that we also carefully look at race allocation while at the same time not violate
  discrimination laws. We have two competing laws between the State and Federal and we try
  best to try to demographically cure and not polarize any racial category and work to the best
  efforts to maximize the majority minority while not specifically saying we are only doing
  mapping because we are here for the Hispanics. It’s a delicate balance and we have to factor
City Council Minutes  3  January 25, 2022
   everything in. Race and ethnicity are not pointed out under the Fair Maps Act as well as
  where Council Members residency. The Supreme Court says if the primary characteristics are
  met it’s absolutely irrelevant where Officials live. We don’t focus on race in districting, but
  we recognize it hence the underlying maps we showed showing the racial and ethnic
  categories to make sure we don’t strangle them and keep them polarized.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked if someone can let Mr. Moore know why his 2018 Map does not
  qualify.

2.  General Plan Amendment GPA2021-38 - a City-Initiated Comprehensive Update to
  the Economic Development Element of the City of Mission Viejo General Plan

  Continued the Item and Public Hearing to the March 8, 2022 City Council Meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Stated that she was making a complaint against City Attorney Bill Curley in
regard to an interaction she had during the Zoom meeting about The Gardens project proposal last
night. She outlined the interaction between them.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Voiced his concerns on The Garden Plaza proposal and suggested that the
Council institute a moratorium over the urban core area. Stated he is in favor of the acquisition of
the Stein Mart property but understands why Value Rock’s proposal has caused adjacent and
affected property owners both commercial and residential to become nervous.

Al Vaitkus, M.V.: Voiced concerns over the small planes flying over Mission Viejo and the impact
of leaded fuel. Stated he was going to speak to environmental groups.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

3.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 11, 2022, as
  presented.

4.  Check Register Dated December 24, 2021 in the Amount of $711,826.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated January 7, 2022 in the Amount of $1,274,273.57
City Council Minutes  4  January 25, 2022
   Ratify the accompanying check register.

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

11. Agreements for Disaster-Related Debris Management and Monitoring Services

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to Execute an Agreement with Ashbritt, Inc. (A22-02) for
  Debris Management Services; (2) authorized the City Manager to Execute an Agreement with
  DRC Pacific, Inc. (A22-03) for Debris Management Services; (3) authorized the City Manager
  to Execute an Agreement with Debris Tech, LLC (A22-04) for Debris Monitoring Services;
  and (4) authorized the City Manager to Execute an Agreement with Tetra Tech, Inc. (A22-05)
  for Debris Monitoring Services.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

12. Assignment of Ground Lease for Veterinary Emergency Clinic located at 28085 Hillcrest
  from South Orange County Veterinary Emergency Group, Inc. to Pathway Vet Alliance
  LLC.

  Assistant City Manager presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  5  January 25, 2022
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Transfer the assignment of the Ground Lease Agreement (A22-06) that is in good standing
  as agreed upon by both City and South Orange County Veterinary Emergency Group, Inc.
  (SOCVEG) to Pathway Vet Alliance, LLC, with amendments pursuant to the terms of the
  Ground Lease.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

14. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Bucknum.

15. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum had no report.

16. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley.

17. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Sachs.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell had no further comments.

Council Member Kelley

City Council Minutes  6  January 25, 2022
 Council Member Kelley announced that the Red Cross has indicated there is a severe blood shortage
and they are desperately seeking donors. The City held a blood drive on January 18 which was
very successful there were 51 donors and they collected 53 units of blood which will help up to 159
people. Each unit of blood helps 3 people. She stated that she had planned to attend, but had
COVID at that time. She is scheduled to donate blood on February 2 and she encourages residents
to go to www.redcross.org to view upcoming blood drives. Lastly, she reported on the Toy Drive
with our adopted Marine Battalion on December 16, and showed photos taken at the event. She
thanked the community for their donations.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that he attended the Chamber of Commerce Day Breakers this
morning at the Norman P. Murray Center. He commented that the Murray Center looks really
beautiful. He then had lunch at the Oso Creek Golf Course. He announced that tomorrow morning
the Rotary Club will be meeting at the golf course 7:10 a.m. if anyone wants to drop by and have
breakfast. Lastly, he announced he went to the Mission Viejo Post Office for the last two weeks at
9:30 am he picks up the trash. He contacted Congresswoman Katie Porter to complain but has
heard no response. He asked the City Manager in the next month or two to have Caltrans give a
presentation on the I-5 Freeway.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said at the last meeting one of Mayor Bucknum’s objectives was to be kind
to each other. He stated that he was struck by both the public comments and the comments during
the public hearing on the district maps. Expressed that we are very divided. He doesn’t appreciate
the attacks on staff and the Council. Lastly, he said we were elected by the City at large and we are
the city’s representatives and we will continue to perform our duties until our term is up or we are
up for re-election.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum wanted to ensure the residents regarding a forum on the Sober Living Homes
throughout the city. City Manager Dennis Wilberg gave an update and will provide a more detailed
report at the next meeting. She stated that she received a lot of feedback on the scoping meeting
held last night regarding the Garden Plaza and asked if staff has a next step of a possible scoping
meeting to address some of the things that were not fully addressed at that meeting. City Manager
Wilberg stated they are working on either an additional scoping meeting or community outreach
meeting. Mayor Bucknum stated to the residents that we are listening to you and are supportive of
good projects. Lastly, she announced she will not be at the next meeting due to a family matter she
needs to attend to.

At the hour of 7:49 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 8, 2022, at 5:00 p.m.
